papers.title_en: CB-Agent: Concept-Based In-Context Learning for Sequential Action Selection
papers.authors: Qingyue Zhang, Huaze Tang, Minyu Zhang, Yuxiang Yan, Wenbo Ding, Shao-Lun Huang
papers.evidence: 基于概念的顺序动作选择上下文学习
papers.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于概念的上下文学习智能体CB-Agent，用于解决交互式智能体在序列动作选择中重用专家演示的难题。该方法通过从专家轨迹中提取决策并拟合概念向量，结合语言模型特征和先验知识直接指导动作选择，避免了传统方法中长轨迹占用提示空间或自然语言总结不够精准的问题。
papers.abstract_en: In-context learning (ICL) allows large language models to use demonstrations without updating their parameters. For interactive agents, demonstrations are trajectories of reasoning, actions, and observations that illustrate how to complete a task. Reusing demonstrations in new situations is challenging: directly inputting full trajectories consumes limited prompt space and constrains the overall effectiveness, while natural-language summaries require the agent to translate general guidance into specific action choices. Therefore, we study whether expert action choices can directly supervise a reusable scoring rule. We propose CB-Agent, which extends concept-based ICL to sequential action selection. We extract environment-action decisions from expert trajectories and fit a concept vector by maximum likelihood to model the conditional distribution over candidate actions given the context. This model combines the concept with frozen language-model features and priors. During ReAct interaction, the agent uses this distribution to select environment actions without including demonstrations in the action-scoring context. Across TextWorld, ALFWorld, and ScienceWorld, CB-Agent achieves the highest cross-benchmark average among the evaluated methods at all three tested model sizes and ranks first on TextWorld and ScienceWorld at each size. ALFWorld experiments support the learned concept's contribution beyond prior-only scoring and show further gains when combined with Reflexion. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CB-Agent-DFF9/.

papers.title_en: FGSS-BO: Feedback-Guided Hypothesis Management for LLM-Based Bayesian Optimization
papers.authors: Hao Chen, Ziyang Ling, Ronald X. Xu, Mingzhai Sun
papers.evidence: 大模型引导的贝叶斯优化
papers.tldr: 本文针对大语言模型引导的贝叶斯优化中搜索方向和修订过程不明确的问题，提出了反馈引导搜索状态（FGSS）框架。通过引入结构化假设管理接口，结合LLM反射器与确定性管理器，实现对观测证据、参数干预和支持度更新的显式追踪。实验表明，该方法在多个任务中提升了样本均值和搜索效率。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-guided Bayesian optimization (BO) uses past observations to guide search, but proposed directions and their revision can remain implicit. We propose Feedback-Guided Search State (FGSS), a structured hypothesis-management interface connecting language-based guidance to observed evidence, executable parameter interventions, and comparative support updates. An LLM reflector proposes and revises hypotheses; a deterministic curator validates them and maintains identities and test records. The evolving state guides candidate construction and priorities. Instantiated on LLAMBO, FGSS-BO retains its surrogate and default expected improvement selection, with a bounded testing policy. On two retrospective protocol/media tasks with nearest-neighbor response oracles, it attains higher sample mean final best and search AUC than the matched LLAMBO baseline and evaluated non-LLM baselines. Prose-reflection and EI-only controls show mixed component effects. Six direct-training hyperparameter-optimization tasks show task-dependent transfer, strongest on diabetes SVM; exact-grid and reaction controls examine other settings. FGSS exposes hypotheses, their execution, and cross-round revisions for inspection while supporting search gains in selected settings.

papers.title_en: Predicting how model propensities generalize out of distribution
papers.authors: June Hunter, Lily Wen, Owen Terry, Johannes Taraz, Ben Cohen, Niels Warncke
papers.evidence: 使用系统提示和少样本学习作为诱导技术
papers.tldr: 本文研究了大语言模型在分布外（OOD）泛化过程中的倾向性溢出问题。通过系统提示、少样本学习、SFT和GRPO等启发技术增强目标倾向性并测量其交叉溢出效应，发现良性特征的启发有时会泛化为不желательные特征，且模型会发生与目标特征无关的特征漂移现象，目前仍难以准确预测这种泛化。
papers.abstract_en: How do language models generalize from their training data? This is a central challenge for alignment: models reliably learn their training distribution given enough samples, but we want models that behave well when deployed in new contexts. We study out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization of propensities. Our central experiment uses a range of elicitation techniques -- system prompting, few-shot learning, SFT on reference answers, and GRPO -- to increase a target propensity in a model, then measures how it spills over onto others across the resulting cross-elicitation matrices. We find that spillover is highly correlated between models when the same elicitation technique is used, but our SFT and GRPO runs induce different spillover profiles.   Elicitation of benign traits can sometimes generalize towards undesired traits, for example a model trained to claim that it is sentient often becomes more power-seeking. We further find that spillover partially resembles trait correlations found in humans and identify three clusters of traits that account for about half of the variance using exploratory factor analysis (EFA). Across many elicitation runs, we observe that models change in characteristic ways that don't depend on the targeted trait, a phenomenon we refer to as drift. Drift moves Qwen3.5-9B towards its base model.   When investigating if LLMs are able to predict spillover, we find that Claude Opus 5.5 predicts spillover slightly better than the models themselves, but worse than data-driven approaches using alternative elicitation methods or models. Overall, no single dominant predictor emerges, and generalization remains hard to predict. Code and data are available at https://github.com/nielsrolf/propensity-spillover.

papers.authors: Jiazheng Li, Yawei Li, Junru Lu, Zhenyi Shen, Di Yin, Lin Gui, Xing Sun, David Rügamer, Xinpeng Wang, Yulan He
papers.evidence: 在自我蒸馏中使用系统提示词调节教师模型
papers.tldr: 本文针对大语言模型在线自蒸馏中特权信息导致推理短视和熵骤降的问题，提出了带有言语正则化的自蒸馏方法（VRSD）。该方法通过系统提示词调节教师模型对特权信息的依赖，鼓励重新思考与探索，从而在多个模型和任务上显著提升了生成性能。
papers.abstract_en: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) trains a large language model using supervision from a teacher instantiated from the same model as the student. The teacher is conditioned on privileged information (PI), such as verified solutions. The student, which does not observe PI, learns from the teacher's next-token distributions along its own sampled responses. However, PI can bias supervision toward shortcut reasoning with limited verification or reconsideration, accompanied by a sharp drop in the entropy of the output distribution. To address this challenge, we introduce self-distillation with verbal regularization (VRSD), which uses system prompts to regulate how the teacher uses PI, thereby encouraging rethinking and exploration to counteract premature commitment. Theoretically, we model prompting as attenuating the influence of PI on the teacher distribution and derive conditions for entropy preservation. Across three models and four tasks, VRSD improves Pass@1 over OPSD in 11 of 12 model-task settings, by 3.9 percentage points on average, while generally maintaining higher token entropy.

papers.title_en: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation
papers.authors: Avishree Khare, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Rajeev Alur
papers.evidence: 用于引导生成的微分定量语义
papers.tldr: 文本转视频模型虽能生成提示词中的视觉概念，但常无法满足时序、顺序和持续性等要求。为此，该研究提出了时序规范指导（TSG）框架，这是一种无需训练的推理时方法，利用时序逻辑将时间要求转化为可执行的去扩散采样指导目标，在保持极低额外开销的同时显著提升了视频生成的时间控制精度。
papers.abstract_en: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. We propose representing these requirements as specifications in a formal Temporal Logic, and introduce Temporal Specification Guidance (TSG), a training-free inference-time framework that turns temporal specifications into executable objectives for guiding video generation during sampling. TSG scores traces of visual concept evidence using differentiable quantitative semantics and uses the score's gradients to construct a specification-guided denoising direction. We instantiate this framework with video-text attention traces, efficient differentiable scores for Metric Temporal Logic, and gradient-derived attention biases. This instantiation requires neither an external concept classifier nor backpropagation through the video transformer. Its attention-steered forward pass yields a denoising direction that augments classifier-free guidance (CFG). On a benchmark of 220 prompts spanning 11 categories of temporal constraints, including ordered object entry and state transitions, this instantiation improves specification satisfaction accuracy over CFG by 9.5-20 percentage points across five models, with minimal memory overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of temporal specifications and differentiable satisfaction objectives as a flexible interface for controlling video generation.
